query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor alloying addition (e.g., controlled amounts of Al and Nb) to the CoCrFeNi matrix will promote the in situ formation of a dual-scale, nanohierarchical microstructure with finely dispersed nanoprecipitates. This engineered structure is expected to adapt its friction protection mechanisms over the full temperature range of room temperature to 800 °C, thereby lowering both the coefficient of friction and wear rate relative to the baseline CoCrFeNi alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with a comparatively coarse grain structure and limited adaptive surface evolution during sliding.
generation.intervention: Microalloy the base CoCrFeNi alloy with minor additions of Al and Nb to induce controlled nanoprecipitate formation and compositional undulation.
generation.conditions: Sliding tests performed in air under representative mechanical loads at temperatures spanning from room temperature to 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: A nanohierarchical architecture composed of ultra-fine (nano-coupled) grains interspersed with homogeneously dispersed nanoprecipitates.
generation.mechanism: At lower temperatures, the nanostructured interface fosters multiple deformation pathways that reduce friction. At higher temperatures, the nanoprecipitates trigger the formation of a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer that minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear, collectively providing an adaptive friction interface protection across the full test regime.
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy should display a significantly lower coefficient of friction (potentially below ~0.3) and reduced wear rates (approaching the order of 10^(-7) mm³/N·m) over the entire temperature range compared to the unmodified CoCrFeNi matrix.
generation.baseline: Unmodified CoCrFeNi alloy that struggles to consistently maintain low friction and low wear at both room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 800 °C.
generation.boundary: The prediction applies under sliding in air, with loads and environmental conditions similar to those reported in prior studies; the effects outside this regime (e.g., in vacuum or under different loads) remain untested.
generation.uncertainty: The precise concentrations of Al and Nb required to optimize the nanohierarchical architecture are uncertain, as is the detailed evolution of the microstructure under dynamic sliding conditions; quantitative performance gains need experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one of the baseline CoCrFeNi alloy and another with a minor addition of Al and Nb. Subject both sets to identical sliding tests in air over temperatures ranging from room temperature to 800 °C under the same mechanical load. Analyze the surface microstructures post-testing using TEM/SEM to confirm the occurrence of a nanohierarchical architecture in the modified alloy.
measurements: Coefficient of friction over temperature range
Wear rate (mm³/N·m) across the temperature range
Microstructural characterization (grain size distribution, presence of nanoprecipitates, formation of nanocrystalline glaze layers)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the microalloyed CoCrFeNi does not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in friction coefficients and wear rates compared to the baseline, or if the anticipated nanohierarchical microstructure (nanoprecipitates and nano-coupled grains) does not develop, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Remarkable Wear Resistance in a Complex Concentrated Alloy with Nanohierarchical Architecture and Composition Undulation

Abstract: AbstractSustained wear damages on the sliding surfaces of alloys are generally the culprit responsible for the failure of various mechanical systems. Inspired by high-entropy effects, here we deliberately deploy nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation in a Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 complex concentrated alloy, which yields ultralow wear rate within the order of 10−7 to 10−6 mm3/Nm between room temperature and 800 °C. Such remarkable wear resistance heretofore represents one of the highest wear resistance reported for the bulk alloys or composites, and originates from the multi-type adaptive friction interface protection governed by intrinsically nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates. This cooperative heterostructure releases gradient frictional stress in stages upon wear at room temperature through the coexistence of multiple deformation pathways while activating a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer upon wear at 800 °C to minimize adhesive and oxidative wear.
